content: 1. The combination of netupitant/palonosetron with apomorphine is contraindicated due to an unspecified interaction mechanism. Profound hypotension and loss of consciousness have been reported when 5HT3 antagonists are co-administered with apomorphine. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and caution should be exercised. 3. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, and no dosage adjustment is necessary when co-administered with atazanavir. However, close monitoring is advised. 4. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be co-administered with avapritinib. 6. Netupitant/palonosetron increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. Monitor closely. 7. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Chronic use of strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided in patients taking netupitant. 8. Netupitant/palonosetron increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, reduce the brexpiprazole dose to one-quarter of the usual dose. Monitor closely. 9. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 10. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients transferring from transmucosal buprenorphine co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors to ensure adequate plasma levels. If toxicity occurs, transition back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. 11. Netupitant/palonosetron increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 12. Netupitant/palonosetron increases capivasertib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the capivasertib dose if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 13. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Chronic use of strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided in patients taking netupitant. 14. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Citalopram and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Clomipramine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but no dosage adjustment is required. 19. Cobimetinib levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg daily and resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 20. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Daridorexant levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Limit the daridorexant dose to 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Deflazacort levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 26. Desipramine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Desvenlafaxine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Diazepam buccal levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for adverse reactions due to decreased diazepam elimination. 30. Diazepam intranasal levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for adverse reactions due to decreased diazepam elimination. 31. Doxepin and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Drospirenone levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 33. Duloxetine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Elacestrant levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A4 substrates if needed. 37. Eletriptan and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Encorafenib levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose by half and resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 39. Entrectinib levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 41. Escitalopram and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Estradiol vaginal levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary and monitor closely. 46. Netupitant/palonosetron decreases the effects of fenfluramine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely if co-administered, as serotonin receptor antagonists may reduce fenfluramine efficacy. 47. Fentanyl levels are increased by netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 48. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
